model: Underlying profit capitalisation at cost of equity ex finance income, plus net cash at face (engine route), with blended exit P/E and exit P/B terminal

inputs.sbc_source: None: H1 FY2026 interim note 12 states there were no potential ordinary shares outstanding (no options, awards or convertibles); no share-based payment expense in FY2025 AR or H1 FY2026 interim. SBC-zero market; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:05Z (Yahoo regularMarketTime, Friday regular-session close; HKEX closed over the weekend)
inputs.share_count_basis: 9,484,494,433 shares in issue at 31 Dec 2025 (H1 FY2026 interim note 21, after 334.4m scrip shares issued 2 Dec 2025 at HK$9.77) PLUS ~112m estimated scrip shares for the HK15c interim dividend paid 23 Apr 2026 (HK$1,423m declared x 83% scrip take-up observed on the 2025 final dividend [3,267/3,935] / ~HK$10.5 issue price) = ~9,597m. No dilutive securities. NOTE: Metrics.csv shares_outstanding (9,204.6 for H1 FY2026, 8,886.7 FY2025) is the weighted-average EPS denominator, not shares in issue -- the period-end count is ~3% higher. Held FLAT over the horizon: scrip issuance (~3.5-4%/yr) is an exchange among existing holders of a dividend for new shares at market price while the company retains the cash; the full stream is already credited to the current share base, so compounding the count as well would charge the retained earnings twice.
inputs.stream_basis: The capitalised stream is underlying profit attributable to the Company's shareholders (company definition: reported attributable profit excluding unrealised investment-property fair-value changes of the Group, associates and JVs, net of deferred tax and NCI, including realised revaluation gains on disposal) MINUS after-tax interest on bank deposits. It is post-tax, post-NCI, post-interest-expense, and includes the attributable share of associate/JV profits and interest on advances to associates/JVs (those advances are operating funding of the development JVs and stay out of the bridge). FY2026 underlying profit HK$4,789m (FY2025/26 results announcement as summarised in Analysis.json; FY2025 5,118, FY2024 5,171). Bank-deposit interest FY2026 estimated HK$1,800m pre-tax (H1 FY2026 actual 939 per interim note 5; H2 assumed ~860 on lower HIBOR) x (1-16.5% HK profits tax) = 1,503 after tax, stripped per the excluded-income/matching-asset rule because net cash is added at face. FY0 ex-cash stream = 4,789 - 1,503 = 3,286 (FY2025 on the same basis ~3,320). Engine fields: revenue = ex-cash underlying profit, EBITDA margin 100%, SBC/D&A/capex/tax/WC 0. reported_fcf here holds underlying profit (the company's stream), NOT cash FCF; cash FCF (FY2025 3,412; FY2024 653; FY2023 -849) swings with land purchases and pre-sale deposit timing and is not the value stream for a developer.
inputs.net_cash_basis: 31 Dec 2025 (H1 FY2026 interim, chairman's statement p.8 and balance sheet): time deposits and restricted bank deposits 47,990 + bank balances and cash 5,211 = 53,201; bank borrowings 832 current (FY2025 1,799; context pivot carries 1,799) -- the company quotes total borrowings HK$1,799m and net cash HK$51,402m, which is used. Less the ~HK$242m cash portion (17%) of the interim dividend paid Apr 2026 (its scrip portion is in the share count) -> net_debt -51,160. HK$277m of time deposits are pledged (immaterial). The FY2026 final dividend (HK43c, ~HK$4.1bn, ~83% expected in scrip) is paid out of H2 FY2026 earnings that are neither in the Dec-2025 cash nor in the FY2027+ stream; treated as roughly offsetting and ignored. Cash is added at FACE: it is HKD/USD deposits, not trapped or offshore, and the company has run net cash for a decade. The market's persistent discount on this cash (family control, scrip-heavy payout, cash earning HIBOR rather than the cost of equity) is the main bear axis and is reflected in the bear exit multiple, not by haircutting the bridge.
inputs.lease_treatment: Immaterial: lease liabilities HK$37m current + small non-current; lease principal ~HK$42m/yr is inside underlying profit via depreciation/interest. No adjustment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Stream is attributable-only (underlying profit attributable to shareholders); NCI equity HK$465m is not deducted again. Amounts due to NCI (2,127) and to/from associates and JVs are operating JV funding and stay with the stream.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in HKD (pegged to USD): risk-free ~4.0% (US 10y ~4.1%, HK Exchange Fund 10y ~3.7-3.9%), ERP 5.5%, beta ~0.82 for an unlevered (net-cash) HK developer/landlord -> ~8.5%. Same rate in all three scenarios: HK-concentration, office oversupply and family-control risk are carried in the flows and exit multiples (risk charged once). Net cash is not discounted at all (added at face).
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: Sino Land is a diversified HK property developer AND investor (FY2025 consolidated revenue ~36% property sales, ~34% rental, ~12% hotels, ~17% management services) with HK$67.8bn of IAS 40 investment properties, HK$23bn of associates/JVs and HK$51.4bn of net cash. Per dcf-methods SKILL.md it straddles the 'REIT / property trust' row (capitalise a post-interest distributable stream at cost of equity) and the 'inventory-heavy developer' row (blended NTA exit-P/B and earnings exit-P/E). An owner-FCF EV DCF is wrong here: reported net income is polluted by IP revaluations (FY2025 net 4,019 vs underlying 5,118), cash FCF swings with land banking and pre-sale timing, and associate/JV development profit (~40% of group-wide sales) only reaches consolidated cash as dividends/advance repayments. Consistent with the HK developer peers already valued in this folder (0012.HK Henderson, 0016.HK SHKP, 0004.HK Wharf), the stream is company-defined underlying profit capitalised at the cost of equity, with the terminal multiple set as a blend of exit P/E and exit P/B. Departure from those peers, deliberate: Sino holds HK$51bn net cash (~49% of market cap), so the excluded-income/matching-asset rule is applied -- after-tax deposit interest is stripped from the stream and net cash added at face. Capitalising that interest at ~13x instead would value the cash at ~0.35x face. VINTAGE WARNING: the FY2026 annual report (year to 30 Jun 2026, results Aug 2026) is NOT yet extracted; FY0 underlying profit (4,789) comes from the results summary in Analysis.json and the balance-sheet anchors are 31 Dec 2025. Refresh net cash, shares in issue and FY2026 bank interest when the annual is extracted. Book NAV attributable 170,498 (HK$17.8/share on 9,597m); ex-cash book ~119,100 (HK$12.4/share); price/book 0.59x.
inputs.fy0_stream_history: Underlying profit attributable HK$m: FY2017 5,527; FY2018 11,247; FY2019 4,671; FY2020 4,557; FY2021 10,316; FY2022 6,531; FY2023 6,088; FY2024 5,171; FY2025 5,118; FY2026 4,789 (results summary); H1 FY2025 2,241; H1 FY2026 2,220. Finance income (pre-tax): FY2023 1,391; FY2024 2,340; FY2025 2,258; H1 FY2026 988 (939 on bank deposits). Ex-cash underlying has been ~3.3bn for FY2024-26 (2.8% on ~119bn ex-cash book) after falling from 5-9bn in FY2021-23 when development completions and lower deposit rates ran the other way.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (FY2020-FY2025), cross-checked against underlying NPAT 5yr CAGR 2.35%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.5-3.2%) diverges >30% from revenue (-19.3% 3yr / +6.8% 5yr) and reported EPS (-16.0% 3yr / +13.4% 5yr). Expected for a developer: revenue and reported EPS are dominated by completion timing and IP revaluations (FY2020 EPS 0.24 was a revaluation-loss trough, flattering the 5yr EPS CAGR). Equity growth is understated per share by ~4%/yr scrip issuance.
historical_growth.notes: FCF here is reported cash FCF (OCF less capex) -- SBC is zero, so owner and reported coincide before the interest strip; it is not the valuation stream (see inputs.stream_basis). Underlying profit has fallen from HK$10.3bn (FY2021) to ~HK$4.8bn (FY2026), and per share faster because of scrip dilution.

base.narrative: Ex-cash underlying profit HK$3.55bn in FY2027 (HK$6.6bn of contracted-but-unrecognised sales plus La Mirabelle's HK$4.6bn launch recognising over FY2027-28; HK development margins bottoming per sell-side), HK$3.75bn FY2028, HK$3.9bn FY2029 as hotels and management services keep growing and rental stabilises, then 3% fading to 2.5%. This is a modest recovery to roughly the FY2024-25 ex-cash level plus inflation, not a return to the FY2021-23 development peak.
base.terminal_cap_multiple_rationale: Blend of 12x exit P/E (HK developer/landlord mid-cycle) and ~0.45x exit P/B on ex-cash book (~HK$130bn by FY2036 -> ~HK$58bn, ~12.5x the FY2036 stream), rounded up to 13x for the recurring rental/hotel share. Gordon at 8.5%/2.0% is 15.7x, so the cap binds.

bull.narrative: HK residential upcycle on Fed/HIBOR cuts sustains La Mirabelle-style take-up across the To Kwa Wan, Yau Tong and LOHAS Park Package 13 launches at recovering margins; tourism recovery and Kai Tak mega-events lift hotel and mall income; office vacancy peaks in 2027 and reversions turn; the Northern Metropolis (Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen) pilot site starts contributing late in the decade. Ex-cash underlying profit HK$3.9bn / 4.4bn / 4.8bn / 5.0bn, then 3.5%.
bull.terminal_cap_multiple_rationale: 15x exit P/E, consistent with ~0.6x exit P/B on ex-cash book as the NAV discount narrows in an upcycle. Gordon at 8.5%/3.0% is 18.7x; cap binds.

bear.narrative: HK office vacancy goes above 20% by 2027 and retail reversions stay negative as Mainland visitors shift to experiences and residents travel out; development margins stay compressed and the land bank is replenished at full prices, so ex-cash underlying profit falls to ~HK$3.0bn and stays near HK$2.9-3.0bn; the family keeps hoarding cash at HIBOR and paying mostly in scrip, so the market never closes the NAV discount. 1% growth thereafter.
bear.terminal_cap_multiple_rationale: 10x exit P/E, ~0.25x exit P/B on ex-cash book (at the trough of HK developer discounts). Gordon at 8.5%/1.0% is 13.5x; cap binds.

scenario_narratives.base: Development profit recovers modestly from the FY2026 trough as contracted sales and La Mirabelle are recognised; rental flat-to-slightly-up, hotels and management services grow; ex-cash underlying profit ~HK$3.9bn by FY2029 then grows with nominal GDP. Net cash HK$51bn added at face. Exit at 13x earnings (~0.45x ex-cash book).
scenario_narratives.bull: HK housing upcycle plus tourism and office recovery; ex-cash underlying profit reaches HK$5bn by FY2030 and the NAV discount narrows to ~0.6x ex-cash book (15x exit).
scenario_narratives.bear: Structural HK office/retail oversupply and compressed development margins hold ex-cash underlying profit near HK$3bn; the cash pile keeps earning HIBOR under family control and the stock exits at 10x (~0.25x ex-cash book).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% house default): underlying profit has fallen in four of the last five years, HK office/retail oversupply is structural rather than cyclical, and the dividend now exceeds underlying EPS with the gap funded by scrip. Base 50%: HK$6.6bn of contracted sales and the La Mirabelle launch underpin FY2027-28. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs a housing upcycle, an office recovery and a narrowing NAV discount at the same time. The HK$51bn net cash, held identically in every scenario, limits downside, which is why the bear case is not weighted higher.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sino Land is valued as two things: HK$51bn of net cash at face (~HK$5.3/share) and an operating property business (development, rental, hotels, management) worth its ex-cash underlying earnings capitalised at an 8.5% cost of equity with a 10-15x exit. The stock trades at 0.59x book NAV; the earnings-based value of the operating assets is ~0.4-0.5x their book value, because they earn only ~2.8% on ex-cash book. The NAV discount is therefore treated as earned, not as a mispricing to be closed.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY2026 annual report not yet extracted: FY0 underlying profit, deposit interest and net cash are estimates/Dec-2025 anchors
Cash valued at face, though the market has persistently discounted it under family control with a mostly-scrip payout
Development profit is lumpy: one or two big completions can move a year's stream by +/-30%
HK office vacancy (16-18%, forecasts >20% by 2027) and retail reversions
HIBOR: lower rates cut deposit income (stripped here) but support residential demand and cap rates
Scrip dilution ~3.5-4%/yr redistributes value from cash-electing to scrip-electing holders at prices below book
